A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multilevel neural simulation-based inference work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material relocated between the main text and supplements.

before.justification: v1 reports original inference experiments on the g-and-k distribution, Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process, toggle-switch model, and CAMELS data, plus training-time measurements and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds experiments on unequal parameter dimensions, simulation-budget allocation, and gradient-adjustment components.

M1.justification: The MLMC objective, seed coupling, gradient rescaling, and conditional projection are retained. Algorithm 1 corrects its nonconflicting branch to preserve the summed correction gradient h_c rather than h_1. This is a limited correction to the stated pseudocode; a corresponding implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: The four original benchmark domains remain. Appendix B.3.1 adds an OU inference scenario in which the high-fidelity simulator has an additional unknown initial-value parameter, whereas v1 fixes that initial value. This extends coverage to unequal parameter dimensions across fidelities.

E2.justification: The new OU failure-case comparison in Table 2 includes high-fidelity-only NPE trained on 100 samples alongside ML-NPE and TL-NPE. v1's corresponding OU accuracy comparisons primarily compare ML-NPE with TL-NPE, with a much larger NPE serving as the reference posterior.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 revises stated training counts from (11000,1000) to (1100,100) for TL-NPE and from (10000,1000) to (1000,100) for ML-NPE; reference-NPE training falls from 100000 to 10000. Toggle-switch n2 changes from 300 to 100, and its stated cost from 60300 to 603000. These reported corrections do not establish reruns of the retained plots. New experiments also introduce alternative approximately equal-cost allocations and four gradient-adjustment controls.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's sensitivity plots and gradient-loss illustration, v2 adds an unequal-dimensional OU failure analysis, a comparison of three simulation-budget allocations, and component ablations separating rescaling, projection, their combination, and neither. These substantially expand testing of applicability, allocation choices, and optimisation mechanisms.

E5.justification: The stated 10 repetitions for timing and 20 for OU, existing distribution plots, and posterior median-absolute-deviation reporting are retained. New tables continue mean/standard-deviation summaries already used in v1; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure, significance test, or increase in repetitions is stated.

E6.justification: The original benchmark plots and timing values are retained, but Tables 2–4 add substantial numerical evidence. Table 2 reports OU NLPD of -0.18 for ML-NPE versus -1.21 for high-only NPE, despite slightly better KLD, 0.98 versus 1.05. Table 3 adds allocation results, and Table 4 reports component-ablation results, including toggle-switch MMD of 0.26 with both adjustments versus 0.59 with standard training.

T1.justification: Theorem 2 and its appendix proof correct the allocation cost factor from C_l+C_{l+1} to C_l+C_{l-1}, aligning it with the stated simulation cost. v2 also displays the MC variance bound implied by Theorem 1. The central variance bounds and overall proof approach remain.

C1.justification: The abstract's central accuracy-at-fixed-budget claim is unchanged. The introduction and conclusion narrow v1's unqualified claim of requiring no additional hyperparameters to requiring no additional fidelity-related hyperparameters, while retaining the main multilevel and computational-efficiency contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive qualifications: it tentatively attributes the new OU failure to optimisation instability, explains allocation choices through differences between successive simulators, and notes that gradient adjustment can increase metric variance when standard training already suffices. The earlier seed-matching and training-overhead limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies the small positive epsilon used in Algorithm 1 and documents the added OU initial-value prior, alternative sample allocations, and settings inherited by the ablations. Existing network specifications, hardware, learning rate, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Dinh et al. (2014), Papamakarios et al. (2017), Liang et al. (2022), and contemporary cosmological multifidelity studies by Saoulis et al. and Thiele et al. (2025). These refine background and contextual positioning without replacing the principal relationship to MLMC and transfer-learning SBI.

P1.justification: The introduction, NPE background, optimisation explanation, and conclusion receive localized rewrites. The former optimisation appendix is redistributed into Section 3 and Appendix B.6, while proofs and experimental appendices are renumbered. The six-section main narrative and much of the existing prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a substantially different document format, including a redesigned title/author block, smaller typography, and reflowed equations and floats. Algorithm 1 moves into the main text, three tables are added, appendix figures are rearranged, gradient graphics are relabelled, and Figure 1 gains an Overdensity color-bar label.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's largely illustrative optimisation evidence, v2 adds quantitative component ablations, tests allocation choices, and openly reports an OU failure case. Corrections also improve consistency of the cost formula and reported budgets. These provide a limited net improvement in validation and clarity, although Tables 3 and 4 leave an unexplained toggle-switch MMD difference, 0.16 versus 0.26, for nominally matching full-method settings.
